core_obligations: Derive the direct implication (base change of locally separated is locally separated) from the cited Morphisms of Spaces lemma (proof lines 2302-2305).
Unpack the hypothesis: each base change X_i \to Y_i locally separated means each \Delta_i : X_i \to X_i \times_{Y_i} X_i = Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X) is an immersion (proof lines 2307-2317).

Note the base change of the fppf covering {Y_i \to Y} gives an fppf covering of X \times_Y X, that each \Delta_i is the base change of \Delta : X \to X \times_Y X, and conclude via lemma-descending-fppf-property-immersion that \Delta is an immersion, i.e. f is locally separated (proof lines 2318-2328).
proof_roadmap: Handle the direct implication by base-change stability.
Reformulate local separatedness of the base changes as immersiveness of their diagonals.
Descend the immersiveness of the diagonal along the fppf covering.
difficulty_reason: The proof has two genuine halves: the direct implication from the cited base-change stability of local separatedness; and the converse, which identifies each base-changed diagonal \Delta_i : X_i \to X_i \times_{Y_i} X_i = Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X) as an immersion, observes that base change turns the fppf covering {Y_i \to Y} into an fppf covering of X \times_Y X, and descends the immersion property of \Delta from the covering via the diagonal form of the fppf descent lemma. The diagonal reformulation of local separatedness driving the descent is the substance.
